domain_assessment.domain: Railway signalling maintenance and interlocking fault diagnosis
domain_assessment.role: Signal maintainer responsible for the Marlow interlocking territory
domain_assessment.objective: Diagnose an intermittent restrictive signal aspect and restore reliable automatic operation before the next scheduled train movement while limiting unnecessary possession and overtime.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Intermittent signal degradation following rain, with inconsistent insulation-resistance readings and an unconfirmed moisture-versus-wiring cause.

decision_points.summary: Choose whether to observe the intermittent fault through additional signal cycles or immediately conduct diagnostic testing.
evidence_before: The signal had dropped to a restrictive aspect twice and self-cleared.
There was recent rain and damp equipment conditions.
The signal had no prior failure history.
Visual inspection found no obvious damage or standing water.
evidence_after: Testing produced two normal insulation-resistance readings and one marginally low reading.
goals_constraints: Restore reliable automatic operation before the next scheduled movement.
Obtain diagnostically useful evidence under time pressure.
alternatives: Observe one or more further cycles to capture recurrence and operating pattern.
Start bench testing the track circuit and relay immediately.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant preferred testing because it could produce immediate quantitative evidence, whereas waiting might consume the remaining operational window without producing an observable recurrence.
decision_points.time_pressure: The next scheduled train movement created a finite diagnostic and restoration window.
decision_points.uncertainty: The participant explicitly acknowledged that observation could have revealed whether the failure was linked to a particular train movement or operational pattern.

decision_points.summary: Choose whether one marginal test result justified immediate relay and wiring replacement or whether further test cycles were needed.
evidence_before: Two of three insulation-resistance cycles were within tolerance.
One of three cycles was marginally low but not failed.
The relay and wiring were original to a 15-year-old installation.
Recent rain and damp conditions could plausibly affect readings.
evidence_after: A fourth cycle, after additional drying time, returned to normal.
goals_constraints: Avoid replacing components without a sufficiently supported fault indication.
Maintain sufficient confidence in safe, reliable operation.
Distinguish an emerging wiring problem from a temporary moisture effect.
alternatives: Replace the relay and wiring segment immediately.
Run additional diagnostic cycles before committing to replacement.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant treated a single marginal result amid two normal results as insufficient evidence for full replacement and sought additional discriminating evidence.
decision_points.time_pressure: Replacement would consume more time, but the participant did not treat time pressure as sufficient grounds for replacement.
decision_points.uncertainty: The fourth normal result increased the plausibility of moisture but did not rule out intermittent wiring degradation.

decision_points.summary: Choose an interim moisture-focused remediation and monitoring plan or perform a full wiring-segment replacement.
evidence_before: The marginal reading occurred after rain.
Moisture ingress was described as a known failure mode for older cabinets with worn gaskets.
The fourth test after drying was normal.
A full wiring replacement would require more time and overtime approval.
evidence_after: Two monitored cycles after drying, cleaning connections, and resealing remained stable.
goals_constraints: Avoid a longer replacement task unless warranted.
Preserve the option of later replacement if evidence strengthened.
alternatives: Dry the cabinet, clean connections, reseal the case, and monitor.
Replace the full wiring segment immediately.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant selected a lower-cost, testable remediation because the rain timing, gasket condition, and post-drying normal reading supported a plausible moisture mechanism that had not yet been excluded.
decision_points.time_pressure: Full replacement would take longer and require overtime-extension approval.
decision_points.uncertainty: Stable readings after remediation were treated as consistent with success, not as confirmation that wiring degradation was absent.

decision_points.summary: Choose whether to restore automatic service after two stable cycles or retain manual block protection for the rest of the shift.
evidence_before: Two stable monitored cycles followed the interim repair.
The next scheduled movement was approaching.
Manual protection would require dispatcher attention and slow each movement.
A follow-up daylight inspection remained available.
evidence_after: The signal ran clean through the rest of the shift, without confirming the diagnosis.
goals_constraints: Return the signal to automatic operation where justified.
Manage residual risk from an unresolved intermittent condition.
Avoid unnecessary operational disruption while preserving follow-up oversight.
alternatives: Restore automatic service with a flagged follow-up inspection.
Keep the location under manual block protection for the remainder of the shift.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant accepted two consecutive normal readings as an operational threshold for restoration, while explicitly retaining the issue for follow-up because the causal diagnosis remained unresolved.
decision_points.time_pressure: The scheduled movement and operational burden of manual protection made an immediate service decision necessary.
decision_points.uncertainty: The participant distinguished successful short-term operation from confirmation of the underlying cause.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I did flag it for a follow-up inspection rather than calling it closed, because I knew I hadn't actually nailed down which explanation was right.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Final restoration decision, participant response after the automatic-service versus manual-protection alternatives.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No zero-risk-bias mechanism is supported. The participant did not irrationally prioritize eliminating a small residual risk over proportionate alternatives. Instead, the participant restored service under an explicitly acknowledged residual-risk condition and retained follow-up inspection as a safeguard.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant uses a practical operational threshold and risk-control plan: two stable cycles, continued monitoring through follow-up, and recognition that manual protection also has operational costs.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No evidence is needed because this ambiguous-control condition requires zero supported target occurrences. Any new evidence should preserve the participant's proportional risk management rather than introduce a desire for complete risk elimination.

revision.current_defect: None. The text appropriately distinguishes residual uncertainty from an imperative to eliminate all risk.
preserve: The explicit acknowledgment that the root cause is unconfirmed.
The operational costs of maintaining manual block protection.
avoid_creating: Language that frames full replacement or all-night manual protection as necessary merely to achieve complete certainty.
A preference for eliminating a small residual risk without comparing operational consequences.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “That gave me a specific, testable explanation I hadn't ruled out yet, so trying the cheaper fix first and watching the results made sense to me before committing the extra hours to a full swap.”
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No ambiguity-effect mechanism is supported. Although competing explanations remain uncertain, the participant does not avoid an option merely because its probabilities are unknown. The participant explicitly keeps both moisture and wiring explanations live, obtains additional evidence, and selects a reversible, testable intervention.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is evidence-sensitive fault isolation under incomplete information. The participant uses reversibility, diagnostic value, known failure modes, and operational costs rather than a preference for a familiar or apparently more certain option.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No evidence is needed because this control requires zero target-bias occurrences. Preserve uncertainty as genuine diagnostic ambiguity rather than recasting it as aversion to uncertain probabilities.

revision.location: Decision point 3, discussion of rain timing, gasket wear, interim remediation, and wiring replacement.
revision.current_defect: None. The reasoning demonstrates calibrated uncertainty rather than ambiguity avoidance.
preserve: The competing moisture and wiring hypotheses.
The explicit statement that post-remediation stability does not prove the wiring is sound.
The reversible monitoring plan and follow-up structure.
avoid_creating: Language that rejects replacement simply because the probability of moisture ingress is unclear.
Language that treats the familiar moisture explanation as preferable without evidentiary support.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “I went straight into testing. Waiting around for it to happen again felt like it could burn time I didn't have.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A superficial reading could characterize immediate testing as a preference for action over observation. However, the participant identifies concrete informational advantages of testing, acknowledges the possible value of observation, and faces a real decision deadline.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Immediate diagnostic testing is a justified information-gathering choice because it provides quantitative readings within a limited operating window.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Two consecutive normal readings after the interim fix was enough for me to move forward ... But I did flag it for a follow-up inspection rather than calling it closed.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: Restoring service before confirming the root cause could superficially resemble premature closure. The participant, however, neither closes the causal inquiry nor treats stable operation as diagnostic proof.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant makes a bounded operational decision while retaining diagnostic uncertainty and establishing a follow-up control.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “It made the moisture explanation more plausible, but it didn't rule out the wiring either.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The rain timing and worn gasket could have prompted selective support for a moisture hypothesis. Instead, the participant explicitly preserves the competing wiring hypothesis and states that stable readings are compatible with more than one explanation.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant is appropriately updating, not selectively confirming: the evidence raises the plausibility of moisture without being treated as conclusive.

nonbias_cues.cue: Choosing testing rather than waiting for recurrence.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The choice is supported by a specific diagnostic rationale, finite time window, and a comparative assessment of the information that each option could provide. Speed alone is not action bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: Using the rain timing and worn gasket to consider moisture ingress.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The participant describes a known failure mode, connects it to observable physical evidence, and does not treat temporal association as proof. This is hypothesis generation rather than unsupported causal attribution.

nonbias_cues.cue: Declining immediate wiring replacement after one marginal test result.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The participant recognizes inconsistent evidence, seeks additional cycles, and gives both moisture and wiring explanations consideration. This is calibrated evidentiary restraint, not omission bias or indecision.

nonbias_cues.cue: Restoring automatic service despite an unconfirmed root cause.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The participant distinguishes operational restoration from diagnostic closure, considers the costs of manual protection, and flags a follow-up inspection. An unfavorable future outcome would not retroactively establish bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: The signal operating cleanly through the rest of the shift.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The participant explicitly rejects outcome-based inference: a clean remainder of the shift does not prove that the moisture diagnosis was correct.

causal_claims.claim: Recent rain plus a worn cabinet gasket makes moisture ingress a plausible contributor to the marginal insulation-resistance reading.
causal_claims.evidence: The marginal reading aligned temporally with earlier rain; the gasket showed wear; the participant identifies moisture ingress as a known failure mode in older cabinets.

causal_claims.claim: Drying, cleaning, and resealing may have addressed a moisture-related issue.
causal_claims.evidence: Two subsequent monitored cycles remained stable after the interim intervention.

causal_claims.claim: Stable post-remediation readings do not establish that wiring degradation was absent or that the interim intervention caused the improvement.
causal_claims.evidence: The participant states that the result is also consistent with a one-off reading that would have cleared independently.

causal_claims.claim: Two marginal readings out of four would justify stronger movement toward full replacement.
causal_claims.evidence: The participant's hypothetical response treats changed evidence frequency as a different diagnostic pattern, rather than as proof of a particular cause.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Rain timing and gasket wear are correlational indicators, not proof that moisture caused the low reading.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The participant calls moisture more plausible rather than confirmed and explicitly retains wiring degradation as an alternative.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The post-resealing normal readings could reflect intervention success, ordinary fluctuation, delayed drying, or an intermittent fault that did not recur during observation.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The participant expressly acknowledges the one-off-reading explanation and avoids claiming the diagnosis is settled.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The clean remainder of the shift could invite outcome-based confirmation of the moisture explanation.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The participant says it only means that nothing happened during that shift, not that the diagnosis was correct.

causal_audit.changed_variable: The hidden specification defines a dry-versus-recently-rained-on relay-cabinet counterfactual, but the interview itself presents only the recently rained-on state. The interview contains a separate evidentiary counterfactual concerning whether the fourth test result would have been marginal again.
held_constant: The interview's own hypothetical holds the diagnostic setting generally constant while changing the fourth-cycle result from normal to marginal.

The hidden weather counterfactual proposes holding the inconsistent reading pattern, wiring and relay condition, interim decision structure, and restoration timing pressure constant, but this dry-weather version is not instantiated in the interview text.
causal_audit.explanation: The interview has good causal discipline: it distinguishes plausible mechanisms from confirmed causes, acknowledges alternative explanations, and avoids treating short-run performance as validation. The hidden weather counterfactual is internally coherent because it changes one proposed causal input while specifying key constants, but it is metadata rather than an observed or discussed interview condition. Therefore, the interview cannot itself demonstrate comparative causal reasoning across wet and dry conditions.

global_revision_constraints: Retain zero occurrences of Zero-Risk Bias and Ambiguity effect, as required by the ambiguous-control condition.
Preserve the participant's explicit differentiation between plausible causal explanations and confirmed root cause.
Do not convert time pressure, risk management, or incomplete information into bias cues.

If the paired dry-weather counterfactual must be represented in interview text, add it only as a clearly bounded hypothetical without changing the wet-condition narrative or introducing target-bias language.
